fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Open Green Space; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Multiple Structures; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Mark the secondary access point with a reflective marker so responders can locate it quickly at night.
• Keep all gate latches operable from both sides so responders can move between the front and rear of the property without tools.
• Post the property address on the detached structure if it has a separate entrance or is set back from the road.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so emergency apparatus can reach both structures.
• Trim any landscaping along the access drive that narrows the driveway or blocks sight lines for approaching vehicles.
• Keep a clear walking path between the main residence and the detached structure free of stored items or overgrown plantings.
• Mark or identify any gate or fence opening that provides the primary route to the rear of the property.
• If rear access is limited to foot traffic, confirm that at least one gate is wide enough for a stretcher or hand equipment.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Terrain; Multiple Access Routes; Adequate Vegetation Separation; None Visible
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the scattered cluster closest to the structure to create more open space between individual trees.
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly next to or touching the structure.
• Remove low-hanging branches from scattered trees near the structure so fire cannot climb from ground vegetation into the tree canopy.
• Keep the area immediately around the structure clear of shrub growth and dead plant material.
• Maintain open ground between the base of shrubs and the nearest wall or corner of the structure.
